summary: Today, we are announcing a series of updates that give customers frontier-grade security at half the cost. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is our first cybersecurity model, built ground up to find the most challenging vulnerabilities in complex code bases. When combined with MDASH, it delivers world-class performance at 50 percent of the cost of leading models. We are bringing this capability to market through Project Perception, a complete agentic security offering grounded in real-world signals and security workflows. Teams of specialized agents work together to simulate attacks, detect and triage/investigate, and fix and remediate. This is the benefit of building the harness, context/signals, and action space separate from one model family. By combining specialized models and data with the right agents, tools, security context, and harness, we can advance the frontier of cost to outcome. Today, we are announcing a series of updates that give customers frontier-grade security at half the cost. MAI-Cyber-1-Flash is our first cybersecurity model, built ground up to find the most challenging vulnerabilities in complex code bases. When combined with MDASH, it delivers world-class performance at 50 percent of the cost of leading models. We are bringing this capability to market through Project Perception, a complete agentic security offering grounded in real-world signals and security workflows. Teams of specialized agents work together to simulate attacks, detect and triage/investigate, and fix and remediate. This is the benefit of building the harness, context/signals, and action space separate from one model family. By combining specialized models and data with the right agents, tools, security context, and harness, we can advance the frontier of cost to outcome. The harness argument holds at the other end too. The bottleneck just moved. At half the cost, more gets found, and the queue on the receiving end was already the constraint. On the customer side, the effective action space isn’t bounded by what an agent can do. It’s bounded by what the organization can authorize and absorb: the change window, the application with no identified owner, the host no one can reboot. The harness for finding is being built. The harness for absorbing is still the customer’s own.

The challenge hasn't disappeared—it has simply moved to a different stage of the process. As the cost of discovering issues decreases, organizations are able to identify more opportunities for improvement. However, the real constraint is no longer finding the problems; it is the organization's ability to evaluate, approve, and implement the necessary changes. On the customer side, the limiting factor is not what AI or automation can achieve. Instead, it is determined by operational realities such as governance policies, maintenance windows, application ownership, compliance requirements, and infrastructure that cannot be easily modified. In short, the capability to detect issues is advancing rapidly, but the capacity to absorb and act on those insights still depends on the customer's internal processes and readiness.
